_meta.method: HTTP GET https://composio.dev/toolkits/<slug>, 200 = page exists. Slug variants tried per app.
_meta.caveat: A 200 proves a catalogue page exists, not that the toolkit is deep or current. Coverage signal, not quality signal. Slug mismatches would show as false negatives.

The public API (launched July 2026, all plans, clay-api-key header) has no versioned endpoint catalogue, no public base URL and no OpenAPI spec; the richer People & Company API is Enterprise-only and undocumented.
Product is in maintenance mode — Citrix states it does not maintain the API client libraries and tells customers to fork them.
Not an API at all — MIT-licensed CLI. A toolkit means hosting and wrapping the binary, and inheriting its rate-limit/blocking behaviour.
Keys are self-serve after KYC, but jurisdictional restrictions (notably the US) and request signing make this a compliance question as much as an engineering one.
Not a SaaS API — an npm package (@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli) that shells out to headless Chromium. A toolkit means running it, which means sandboxing and a browser dependency.
API reference is served per-tenant at https://YOURDOMAIN.ladesk.com/docs/api/v3/ — there is no public docs URL to crawl, and keys are admin-created.
API keys require a commerce-capable plan (Core/Plus/Advanced/Commerce Advanced); OAuth requires becoming an approved Squarespace developer partner.
API is gated behind higher-tier plans and documentation is thin; pricing and plan names have changed repeatedly.
Credentials are issued inside a licensed customer tenant — no self-serve signup, no sandbox.
App creation is self-serve, but a tenant admin must review and approve each app version before it works in production.

The public REST API and webhooks are Enterprise-only and enabled by an account manager. Ironically the official MCP server (mcp.otter.ai/mcp, live since March 2026) works on every plan including free Basic.
Enterprise contract; an admin must grant the 'API User' permission before a token can be generated.
Two-step review: Trial access after app review (capped at 1,000 requests/day), Standard access requires submitting a video of the app using the OAuth flow.
App Review required for anything beyond tester accounts; the 'Threads use case' must be chosen at app creation.
Sandbox is instant and free, but Production access requires an application/approval and a commercial agreement. 'Items cannot be moved between environments.'
No consumer API. The only programmatic path is Gemini Notebook Enterprise (formerly NotebookLM Enterprise/Agentspace) inside Google Cloud, with service-account/OAuth auth and enterprise contracting.
Requires a licensed B2C Commerce instance and Account Manager access — no free sandbox for outsiders; partner programme in practice.
No public developer documentation found under this name. The underlying NMI gateway does publish public docs, so any toolkit would target NMI's Payment API with merchant-issued credentials.
Paid platform subscription PLUS a separate Direct Data contract, both negotiated with sales. No free tier, no trial, no public endpoint reference, no self-serve signup.
